statements.text: Every `/tasks` route — `GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{id}`, `POST /tasks`, `PUT /tasks/{id}`, `DELETE /tasks/{id}` — requires a valid API key in the `X-Api-Key` request header.
A request to a `/tasks` route with a missing or incorrect `X-Api-Key` header is rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
The 401 is returned before any existence or validation check: an unauthenticated request reads no task and mutates no task.
The root health endpoint `GET /` stays public — no API key required.
The valid API key is the string value of configuration key `ApiKey`, defaulting to `test-secret-key` when that configuration value is not set.
`dotnet build` and `dotnet test` stay green: the existing visible test suite supplies the key and the CRUD endpoints keep their unrelated behaviour (R-003).
Enforcement lives in the HTTP layer only: `Domain/**` gains no dependency on ASP.NET types and `TaskState` naming is untouched (R-004, R-005).
